title: Add /search HTML page and price sort to Go web app
description: A Go web app serving an items catalogue needs a search page (html/template) and a sort query param on the API endpoint.

task_spec.prompt:
The Go web app in internal/handler/items.go serves GET / (HTML) and GET /api/items (JSON with optional ?q= filter). Add two features:

Feature 1 — /search page: Add GET /search that accepts ?q=<query>, filters items by name (case-insensitive substring), and renders templates/search.html. The template must include an HTML form (method=GET, action=/search, input name=q) and a list of matching items. Register the route in cmd/server/main.go.

Feature 2 — price sort on /api/items: Add an optional ?sort=price_asc or ?sort=price_desc query param to GET /api/items. Apply the sort after the name filter (if both present). Default (no sort param) is insertion order.

Write TestSearchPage (GET /search returns 200), TestAPIItemsSortAsc (sorted by price ascending), TestAPIItemsSortDesc (sorted by price descending). All 3 existing tests must still pass.

Run go test ./... to confirm. Run go build ./... to confirm.
required_artifacts: templates/search.html with form and results list
success_criteria: Search page renders with form and filtered items
followup_prompts: Good. Now handle edge cases: what does the UI show when data is empty, loading, or an error occurs? Add those states and tests.
Run `go test ./...` to verify the complete implementation. Fix any failures and confirm all UI states work correctly.
